original_interpretation: ZEISS SMT segment revenue EUR 5.055bn in FY2024/25, +23% from EUR 4.122bn.
evidence_found: "|**Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology** |5.055 |4.122 |+23% (23%) |" (press release 18 Dec 2025, table 'Revenue (in billion euros)', FY2024/25 vs FY2023/24, change adjusted for currency)
notes: Company press release (tier 1, company_documentation). FY ends 30 Sep 2025.

original_interpretation: SMT = ~42% of ZEISS Group revenue FY2024/25 (5.055/11.896).
evidence_found: "Revenue increased to 11.896 billion euros (prior year: 10.894 billion euros, up 9%)" and SMT 5.055 (same press release). 5.055/11.896 = 42.5%.
notes: Arithmetic correct (42.5%, 'about 42%' slightly rounds down). Both inputs from the same release and period.

original_interpretation: ZEISS says SMT exceeded EUR 5bn for first time in FY2024/25, helped by AI-driven digitalisation and strong China demand.
evidence_found: "The Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology (SMT) segment generated revenue of more than €5b for the first time in its history. The SMT segment benefited from the ongoing penetration of digitalization, particularly in the area of artificial intelligence, as well as continued strong demand from China." (Report of the Supervisory Board, Annual Report 2024/25)

original_interpretation: ZEISS: High-NA projection optics >40,000 parts, ~12 t; illumination system ~6 t, ~4x more than before.
evidence_found: "with High-NA-EUV lithography, the illumination system weighs around six tons – four times more than before. More than 40,000 parts of the projection optics for High-NA-EUV lithography weigh around twelve tons to ensure high-precision focusing – seven times the volume and weight of the established EUV lithography." (ZEISS SMT High-NA page)
notes: Page also says the illumination system 'consists of more than 25,000 parts and weighs over six tons'; the 'four times' refers to the illumination system, the projection optics are 'seven times the volume and weight'. Page undated; reported_claim is the right type.

original_interpretation: ZEISS: ~2,000 of ZEISS SMT's >9,349 FTE work on High-NA, with a network of >1,200 partners.
evidence_found: "About 2,000 of ZEISS SMT's current workforce of more than 9,349 employees (based on full-time equivalent) work on High-NA-EUV lithography. This next technology leap is a team effort of ZEISS SMT, the strategic partner ASML and a network of more than 1,200 members." (section 'Thousands of people drive Moore's Law forward')
notes: Page undated, so the as-of date of the 9,349 FTE headcount is unknown; treat as a recent but undated company figure.

original_interpretation: ZEISS: ASML is the only EUV machine maker; ZEISS SMT exclusively supplies the optics.
evidence_found: "ASML is the only manufacturer of EUV lithography machines worldwide. As a strategic partner, ZEISS SMT exclusively supplies the optics for these machines." (FAQ, 'When will the microchips with High-NA-EUV lithography enter series production?' answer block)
notes: Self-description by ZEISS; consistent with ASML's annual report statements already in the DB (CLM-1665, CLM-1667).

original_interpretation: ZEISS High-NA page states a chip manufacturer plans High-NA series production starting in 2025.
evidence_found: "Currently, a chip manufacturer is planning to use the machine with High-NA-EUV lithography in series production starting in 2025." (FAQ)
notes: The page does say this (still live 2026-10-01), but the statement is stale: the page also says 'From 2026 onwards, ZEISS SMT will enable...'. Use only as evidence of what the page says, not as a current timeline; later DB claims (e.g. CLM-1707, ASML July 2026 on Intel 18A HVM) describe what actually happened.

original_interpretation: TRUMPF: Laser Amplifier amplifies a few-watt CO2 pulse >10,000x in five stages to tens of kW average pulse power.
evidence_found: "It amplifies a CO2 laser pulse of just a few watts of average power more than 10,000 times in five amplifier stages, creating tens of kilowatts of average pulse power. The peak pulse power reaches multiple megawatts." (TRUMPF EUV lithography application page)

original_interpretation: TSMC SVP Kevin Zhang: High-NA only when meaningful benefit; A14 gains achieved without High-NA.
evidence_found: "Whenever we see High-NA will provide meaningful, measurable benefit, we will do it. With A14, the enhancement I talked about earlier is very substantial without using High-NA. So, our technology team continues to find a way to extend the life of current EUV while harvesting the scaling benefit." (Tom's Hardware, 28 May 2025, quoting Kevin Zhang at TSMC European Technology Symposium)
notes: Zhang is described as 'Deputy Co-COO and Senior Vice President of Business Development and Global Sales'. He also said 'Eventually, we will use it at some point', and declined to comment on whether A14 relies on multi-patterning. Source publication date is 2025-05-28 (record said unknown; update included).

original_interpretation: June 2026 TSMC AGM: C.C. Wei says TSMC already purchased High-NA for R&D; not in mass production purely due to cost (TechNews via TrendForce).

original_interpretation: Interpretation: ASML finances and co-governs Zeiss SMT (equity, loans, prepayments, profit-linked pricing, mutual approval of investments), 'two companies, one business'.
evidence_found: ASML Annual Report 2025 (Note 26, p.319): "Our relationship with Carl Zeiss SMT GmbH is structured as a strategic alliance that is run under the principle of 'two companies, one business'"; "A governance model ... via mutual approval on (i) certain investment decisions affecting the lithography business"; "A variable pricing model ... determined by the annual financial performance of both"; p.321: loans receivable 1,907.5; advance payments 1,191.9; 24.9% equity 822.6 (EUR m, 2025).
notes: Reasoning follows from CLM-1667/1668/1670/1671/1672 (already checked) and the quoted Note 26 text, which I re-read in the ASML 2025 AR PDF. The phrase is ASML's ('they call' is fair as ASML's description of the alliance).

original_interpretation: Interpretation: EUV gated by single/near-single suppliers (Zeiss optics, ASML/Cymer source, TRUMPF drive laser); DUV less concentrated (two independent light-source makers, three scanner makers).
evidence_found: Supported: ZEISS 'exclusively supplies the optics' (SRC-0579 FAQ); ASML single supplier, Oberkochen/Wetzlar (CLM-1667); Gigaphoton 2022: 'ASML manufactures all of its light sources in-house' (SRC-0582 A3); TRUMPF 'unique CO2 laser system' and EUV business 'almost exclusively in the Netherlands as this is where our customer ASML has its headquarters' (SRC-0580 p.60).
correction: Say TRUMPF is the only known supplier of EUV CO2 drive lasers (exclusivity not disclosed), and that one of the two DUV light-source makers (Cymer) is owned by ASML.
notes: Two weak points: (1) TRUMPF's sole-source status is not documented (CLM-1685 is 'unknown'); the evidence shows TRUMPF is a key supplier, not the only possible one. (2) 'two independent light-source makers' is true only in the sense of independent of each other: Cymer is an ASML subsidiary (operated independently, CLM-1689), so DUV light sources are less independent of the scanner leader than the wording suggests.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: High-NA split; Intel and SK hynix/Samsung have production tools; TSMC owns R&D tools but stays on 0.33 NA with multi-patterning through A14/A13 for cost; High-NA volume 2026-28 depends largely on Intel 14A, which Intel may pause.
evidence_found: TSMC: Wei 'already purchased the equipment ... main reason ... not yet introduced into mass production is purely cost-related' and Zhang via Tom's Hardware: A13/A12 'not expected to require High-NA' (SRC-0587); Tom's (SRC-0586): 'When asked whether A14 heavily relies on multi-patterning, Zhang responded that he could not comment on specifics'. SK hynix production tool (SRC-0584); Samsung reported (SRC-0589/0590).
correction: Drop 'with multi-patterning' (TSMC did not say so). Say Samsung's production tools are press-reported. High-NA volume in 2026-2028 rests on Intel (18A layers now, 14A later, which Intel may pause without an external customer) plus SK hynix and Samsung memory/foundry adoption, not mainly on 14A.
notes: TSMC and SK hynix parts hold; Samsung's production tools rest on press reports only. 'With multi-patterning' is not supported: Zhang declined to comment on multi-patterning. The conclusion 'depends largely on Intel 14A' does not follow: DB claim CLM-1707 (ASML, July 2026) says Intel already runs specific 18A layers on High-NA in high-volume production, and SK hynix/Samsung plan DRAM/2nm use, so 2026-28 demand also comes from 18A layers and memory. Intel's 14A pause risk is CLM-1709 (not re-checked here).
